finding.title: Import the shared MockAuthRepository from test/mocks/mock_repositories.dart instead of 7 duplicated private copies in the account test suite

evidence.quote: class MockAuthRepository extends Mock implements AuthRepository {}

finding.why: A shared, public MockAuthRepository already exists in test/mocks/mock_repositories.dart, but every one of these 7 files (all in this one batch; ~30 across the repo) reinvents an identical private copy. Low runtime risk today (mocktail's Mock base class no-ops unimplemented members via noSuchMethod), but it's needless duplication that a future AuthRepository interface change has to be reconciled against N private near-identical definitions instead of one, and two of the account_picker files additionally duplicate ~100 lines of ProviderScope/fixture wiring between them (account_picker_screen_l1_test.dart's _Fixture/_buildFixture vs account_picker_local_data_missing_test.dart's _buildApp) with no shared harness module.
finding.recommendation: Import MockAuthRepository from test/mocks/mock_repositories.dart in these 7 files instead of redeclaring it; extract the account-picker widget fixture (registry/userDb/auth/router setup + buildSubject) shared by account_picker_screen_l1_test.dart and account_picker_local_data_missing_test.dart into one harness file.
acceptance_criteria: grep -rn 'class _MockAuthRepository extends Mock implements AuthRepository' learning_tracker/test/features/account returns 0 hits.
The 7 files import test/mocks/mock_repositories.dart's MockAuthRepository and all existing assertions still pass.

finding.title: Move sign-in/account-picker test cleanup into addTearDown so a failed assertion doesn't leak the ProviderContainer/Drift DB
finding.why: Both files call their cleanup helper (_tearDown / _tearDownContainer + registry.close()) as the last statement inside each test body, after several `expect()` calls. If any expect() throws (the exact moment a real regression would be caught), cleanup is skipped and the in-memory Drift registry/userDb connections and ProviderContainer leak for the rest of the suite run — the opposite of TQ-2's 'never share state between tests' guarantee, and the failure that most needs a clean teardown is the one that gets skipped. Sibling files in this exact batch (account_picker_local_data_missing_test.dart's tearDown(), and the notifier tests' addTearDown(container.dispose)) show the correct, already-established pattern.
finding.recommendation: Replace the manual end-of-test _tearDown/_tearDownContainer calls with addTearDown(...) registered immediately after the container/registry/userDb are created, matching account_picker_local_data_missing_test.dart's tearDown() in this same batch.
acceptance_criteria: Cleanup (container dispose, registry.close(), userDb.close()) is registered via addTearDown/tearDown() immediately after creation, not as the final statement of the test body.
A deliberately-failing expect() inserted mid-test still leaves the Drift databases closed.

finding.title: Assert account_picker_local_data_missing_test.dart's expected SnackBar text via the l10n getter, not a hardcoded English literal
finding.rule: Test-fragility / consistency with sibling tests in this batch

evidence.quote:
'This account\'s local data is missing. '
        'Connect to the internet to restore it.',

finding.why: Both C1 and C2 hardcode the expected SnackBar copy as an English literal instead of asserting against `l10n.authLocalDataMissing` the way sign_in_wrong_password_no_callback_test.dart (same batch) asserts against `l10n.authErrWrongPassword`. A future copy edit to the ARB string breaks this test for a cosmetic reason indistinguishable, in the failure output, from an actual regression in the local-data-missing handling logic.
finding.recommendation: Load AppLocalizations in the test (as done elsewhere in this batch) and assert find.text(l10n.authLocalDataMissing) instead of the literal string.
acceptance_criteria: C1/C2 assert against l10n.authLocalDataMissing rather than a literal string.

finding.title: Seed fixed timestamps in sign_in_google_signout_throws_test.dart instead of DateTime.now() in device-account fixtures
finding.why: `_seedAccounts` and the inline local-conflict account both call `DateTime.now()` for createdAt/lastUsedAt. No assertion in this file currently depends on the exact value, so it isn't causing flakiness today, but it's an unseeded wall-clock read in a test file, and the exact sibling problem (device-account fixture timestamps) is already solved with a fixed clock constant one directory over in account_picker_screen_l1_test.dart and sign_in_wrong_password_no_callback_test.dart within this same batch.
finding.recommendation: Replace DateTime.now() with a fixed constant (e.g. `final _kNow = DateTime.utc(2026, 1, 1);`), matching the convention already used by sibling files in this batch.
acceptance_criteria: No DateTime.now() call remains in sign_in_google_signout_throws_test.dart; fixture timestamps use a fixed constant.
